title: Is it NOT this word? using !=
idea: != asks 'are these words different?'. It is True when the words do not match. Predict output using != on strings.

exercises.explanation: != means 'not equal'. For words it is True when they are different, False when they match.

exercises.prompt:
What is the value of this?

"cat" != "dog"
exercises.explanation: The words differ, so 'not equal' is True. != is the opposite of ==.

exercises.prompt:
What is the value of this?

"cat" != "cat"
exercises.explanation: The words are the same, so 'not equal' is False. They ARE equal, so != is False.
"open" is not "closed", so status != "closed" is True and "Come in" prints.

exercises.prompt: Same code, but status = "closed". What prints?
exercises.explanation: Now status != "closed" is False (they match), so the else runs: "Sorry, closed".

exercises.prompt: == and != always give opposite answers for the same two values.
exercises.explanation: Yes - if two words are equal, == is True and != is False, and the other way around. They are mirror opposites.
!= means not equal, so the message runs for any command except "quit".

exercises.prompt: When is != a clearer choice than ==?
options: When you want to act on everything EXCEPT one specific word
exercises.explanation: 'Do this unless the word is X' reads naturally as != X. Choose the operator that matches your intent.
"guest" is not "admin", so != is True and "Limited access" prints.

options: It is True when the words do not match - the opposite of ==
exercises.explanation: != flags a mismatch. Paired with ==, you can test for a word or for anything-but a word.
